newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX loses ground as MOL dips.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX loses ground as MOL dips.

text.p: The Hungarian share market closed 1.73 percent lower on Tuesday despite Monday's sharp rise in the Dow Jones, as MOL weighed down the market, traders said.
The BUX index finished at 5,827.24 points, down 102.63.
Traders attributed the market's cooling to the fact that the trendsetting role of oil company MOL shares has showed signs of weakening.
"The market's positive sentiment we've experienced so far has eased with the MOL fever somewhat fading," one trader said. "The stock had quite a strong selling pressure from abroad."

In the days surrounding MOL's global placement earlier this month the market was overshadowed by heavy trading with mostly rising prices in MOL shares. However, as subscriptions in the domestic offer started on Monday foreigners' enthusiasm waned.
"Foreigners are dumping MOL shares on the market," one trader said earlier today. "The buying side consists mainly of local investors." MOL dipped 25 forints lower at 3,450.
Analysts agreed that as subscriptions in MOL and pharmarmaceuticals Richter are completed later this month the market could face a quiet period.

"Until the MOL and Richter issues are over the buying pressure is likely to remain quite strong, but after that we could see the return of a colder climate," said James Oates, director for central and east Europe at UBS in London.
Elsewhere on the market, traders said buyers had an increasingly better position than sellers.
"In the case of most shares you don't have to pay a much higher price to get a bigger amount of stocks," the Budapest trader said. "However, plastics maker is an exception."
Nevertheless, on Tuesday Pannonplast put on only one forint to end at 8,801 forints.

Companies releasing their first quarter earnings reports closed unchanged although tile maker Zalakeramia posted early gains and traders said the first quarter figures reinforced buyings in the stock.
Zalakeramia closed steady at 7,075 forints, while brewery Soproni which swinged to Q1 profits, ended at 5,800.
